scenarios.testName: turns loopback latency above the Beply timeout into a retryable transport error and recovers locally
scenarios.detection: Beply transport timeout is classified as retryable without an external request escape.
scenarios.recovery: The same loopback provider succeeds after latency is removed.

scenarios.testName: deduplicates provider event IDs and ignores stale failures after capture
scenarios.detection: The duplicate provider event is reported as duplicate and durable side effects remain singular.
scenarios.recovery: The captured payment, allocation and invoice request remain the canonical result.

scenarios.testName: deduplicates provider event IDs and ignores stale failures after capture
scenarios.detection: A failure delivered after capture is observed as stale and cannot downgrade payment state.
scenarios.recovery: No replay is needed because the terminal captured state and exact-once effects are preserved.

scenarios.testName: alerts on an expired worker lease and clears after recovery
scenarios.detection: The operational alert command exits non-zero with stale_worker_leases.
scenarios.recovery: A replacement worker reclaims the lease, delivers exactly once and clears the alert.

scenarios.testName: keeps checkout atomic while Redis is unavailable and reconnects afterward
scenarios.detection: The Redis client rejects the unavailable endpoint while PostgreSQL remains authoritative.
scenarios.recovery: A fresh client reconnects and answers PONG without duplicate checkout or payment effects.

scenarios.testName: retries Beply 503 and 429 outages with durable backoff and issues one invoice after provider recovery
scenarios.detection: HTTP 429 is classified as a provider retry with a future durable availability time.
scenarios.recovery: The same idempotent job completes with one invoice after the provider limit clears.
